title: Rare fossil of T. rex cousin goes on display in New York before heading to auction
description: A fossilized, distant cousin of Tyrannosaurus rex is on display at a Manhattan auction house ahead of its Oct. 27 auction. The Nanotyrannus nicknamed “Jodi” opened for public viewing Tuesday in the lobby of Sotheby’s headquarters on the Upper East Side. Standing 6.5 feet tall and stretching nearly 20 feet long, the rare fossil is one of only three such skeletons known to science. It is projected to fetch $6 million to 9 million. The fossil is named after Jodi Pierson, the Montana rancher who discovered it on her land in 2019. Some people oppose these private sales, saying such finds should be displayed in places that are open to the public and where they can be studied.
